headline: Chinese chip and AI-hardware companies announced sharply higher profits for the first nine months of the year on 16 October.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: company-announced projections from 16 Oct from a handful of firms.
importance_line: It shows Chinese chip suppliers profiting from domestic AI spending, which matters to investors and to officials judging China's chip self-sufficiency, but these are company projections from a handful of firms and Longsys itself says the lift from memory prices is slowing.
summary: The South China Morning Post reports that China's AI infrastructure boom and its push for chip self-sufficiency are lifting earnings at local chip firms, and BigGo Finance's tally of company announcements on 16 Oct 2026 shows the AI chip company Hygon projecting first-nine-month net profit of 2.71 billion to 2.98 billion yuan, up 38 to 52 percent, MetaX swinging to a projected profit of 587 million to 717 million yuan, and the memory maker Longsys projecting a rise of more than 1,800 percent. Longsys said in its announcement that the contribution of rising memory prices to its profit has slowed significantly.
notes: Pool source SCMP (www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3371159/..., HTTP 403) not opened; the SCMP sentence rests on its headline. Facts from a BigGo Finance roundup of 16 Oct 2026 announcements. If the editor wants the SCMP text itself, it must be read separately.
